title: PAIR OF VINTAGE SUNGLASSES - A...
description: PAIR OF VINTAGE SUNGLASSES - AS IS
findings: One photo only. Aviator-style wire sunglasses: gold-coloured (probably gold-filled) frame, pear-shaped green lenses that look like glass, tan plastic brow bar (probably Bakelite), saddle bridge and curled cable temples. The pattern matches the WW2 and 1950s military 'Outdoorsman' or 'shooter' aviators made by Bausch and Lomb (Ray-Ban) and American Optical. No maker's name, B&L, AO, gold-filled stamp or lens etching is legible: the bridge underside, temple arms and lens edges are not shown, and I checked both hinges, the bridge and both lens corners at 3-4x with no marks found. The title gives no maker, material or style. Comparison: a specialist vintage dealer lists marked B&L Ray-Ban and gold-filled 'Outdoorsman' shooter aviators at US$375 each (asking price, vintagesunglassesshop.com/item_vs156.html, seen 16/10/2026), so value depends heavily on whether marks are present at preview.
condition: Sold as is. Frame looks intact with both lenses and both temples; light wear to the gold finish; a small dark spot on the lower part of the left lens; nose pads appear present; the fault behind 'as is' is not visible in the photo.
reason: Under-described vintage cable-temple aviators with brow bar in the B&L Ray-Ban or AO military pattern; unmarked in the photo, so value hinges on marks found at preview.

title: PAIR OF 19th CENTURY HANDCUFFS
findings: Four photos: pair of iron handcuffs of the 'Darby' pattern, with D-shaped hinged cuffs, a cylindrical screw-lock barrel on each, and a short hand-forged chain with a central swivel link. A small keyhole or notch shows in the top end of one barrel; no key is shown. No maker's stamp, crown, broad arrow, number or date is legible on the cuffs, barrels, hinges or chain (checked the barrel ends, hinge areas and chain links at 3-5x). The pattern matches late Victorian Hiatt-type Darbies; for reference a London dealer (St James Collectables) asked GBP255 for a marked Hiatt Darby pair with key, dated 1880-1900 (loveantiques.com listing LA581504, seen 16/10/2026). This pair is unmarked and has no key, so the maker and a true 19th century date are unverified.
condition: Heavy surface rust and pitting under an old dark patina; one cuff looks closed and the other is open with its slotted tongue visible; hinges appear intact; chain complete; no key; string tags tied to the barrels.
reason: Genuine looking Darby pattern police handcuffs, a recognised collectable type, but unmarked and keyless so value is moderate.

title: RYLLTON VINEY SET 3 PENCIL ART...
description: RYLLTON VINEY SET 3 PENCIL ARTWORKS H-15 W-15 CM EACH
findings: Two photos: set of three small graphite studies on paper mounted on white canvases (about 15 cm square), showing mound and structure forms. Photo 2 shows the reverse of one canvas inscribed by hand: 'Ryllton Viney, 2023. Study for a Painting (Earthworks 3), Pencil on Paper Mounted on Canvas, 5 cm (H) x 5 cm (W)'. That signature and date support the catalogue attribution for that canvas; the reverses of the other two were not photographed, so their inscriptions are unseen. Ryllton Viney (b.1944) is a real Launceston based Tasmanian artist with 50+ years of practice, represented in the Queen Victoria Museum and Art Gallery, Artbank, Burnie and Devonport regional galleries and a Glover Prize finalist (art-thoughts-au.com/2021/02/ryllton-viney.html and madelinegordongallery.com.au artist biography, seen 16/10/2026; also listed on printsandprintmaking.gov.au). I found no sale prices for his small studies, so value is uncertain; local Launceston interest is plausible.
condition: Clean unframed canvases, graphite intact, only minor handling marks on the white edges; no damage visible.
reason: Signed and dated 2023 studies by a documented Launceston artist (b.1944) with public collection holdings; thin resale market.
marks_read: 'Ryllton Viney, 2023' on reverse of one canvas; 'Study for a Painting (Earthworks 3)'

title: LLADRO FIGURINE 'GIRL WITH DUC...
description: LLADRO FIGURINE 'GIRL WITH DUCK' AND SMALL LLADRO DUCK FIGURE - H-27.5 CM
findings: Three photos: the large figure is the Lladro 'Girl with Umbrella and Geese' (model 4510, listed by resellers as 1970 to about 1994, retired), which fits the title's 'Girl with Duck', and the small piece is the Lladro 'Ducklings' (01004895, sculptor Juan Huerta, launched 1974: glossy white duck with ducklings in a basket under a blue cloth). Lladro Australia lists the Ducklings new at A$340 (dev2.lladro.com/en_au/ducklings-figurine-en-au-01004895.html, seen 16/10/2026); a Mearto appraisal of a similar girl with umbrella and ducks gave US$60-80 (mearto.com/items/lladro-sculpture-wne, seen 16/10/2026). No base or backstamp is photographed, so the Lladro marks and model numbers are matched by sight only. The grey, lilac and white palette and the modelling are consistent with Lladro, but a Nao or other lookalike cannot be ruled out without a base mark.
condition: No chips, cracks or restoration visible in the three photos; umbrella and handle intact; geese, goslings and basket figures intact; light dust only.
reason: Two Lladro pieces (retired #4510 girl plus Ducklings #4895) that look genuine and undamaged; combined value likely above $100.
